title: How many kinds of rice can a hundred years hold?
description: The video finds the days in a hundred years, then tastes one, two and three kinds of rice each day and compares each total with one lakh. Keeko then raises a hand, thinking that seventy three thousand is almost one lakh and so counts as reaching it.
teaching_notes: One idea: multiply the days in a lifetime by the kinds tasted each day, then subtract to compare the total with one lakh. Ask the class how far each total is from one lakh before the answer appears. Watch for students who say a total that is close to one lakh has reached it.

source: Find the days in 100 years; then the varieties tasted in 100 years at one, two and three varieties a day, and compare each with one lakh
video_script.why: The child can multiply by a hundred and subtract, and has met one lakh as the smallest six digit number.
video_script.substitution: Total kinds tasted equal days in a lifetime times kinds each day, and the gap to one lakh is found by subtracting.
video_script.anchor: Find the days in a hundred years, then the kinds tasted at one, two and three each day, and compare each with one lakh
video_script.wrong_answer: seventy three thousand is almost one lakh
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko treats a total that is close to one lakh as if it had reached one lakh, so two kinds a day seem enough. Almost is not enough, because twenty seven thousand are still missing.
video_script.payoff_line: Only three kinds each day pass one lakh

final_answer.spoken: one lakh nine thousand five hundred

names.Laksh: Eshwarappa's child; wonders about tasting a lakh varieties of rice; says the days in y years are 365 times y
names.Ruhee: Eshwarappa's child; suggests tasting two varieties of rice every day

hold_back: one lakh nine thousand five hundred
maths_rules: days in a year: 365; days in 100 years: 365 × 100 = 36,500
the slip: 73,000 is almost 1,00,000 so it reaches; but 27,000 are still missing
video_script.design: One idea: total kinds tasted equal days in a lifetime times kinds each day, and the gap to one lakh is found by subtracting. Wrong idea: Keeko thinks a total close to one lakh has reached it. The anchor stays all video; the working band builds in the idea part; no hard clear.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>This question is from your book.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Laksh and Ruhee taste new kinds of rice, one, two or three each day, for a hundred years.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Would any of these plans reach one lakh kinds?

beats.on_screen: the anchor holds still and gets an accent underline; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a calendar with three hundred sixty five days in a year; a row of many years; a bowl with the number of kinds tasted each day

marks.m2: the row of years is drawn
marks.m3: the bowl is drawn beside the row

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>A year has three hundred sixty five days, if we ignore leap years.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The days in many years are three hundred sixty five times the number of years.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Tasting some kinds each day, the total is the days times the kinds each day.

beats.on_screen: Given: 365 days in a year, 100 years, 1, 2 or 3 kinds a day

marks.m1: the given line is written in the working band

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Given, there are three hundred sixty five days in a year, and the plan lasts a hundred years.

beats.on_screen: To find: days in 100 years; kinds tasted at 1, 2 and 3 a day; compare with one lakh

marks.m1: the find line is written under the given line

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>We have to find the days in a hundred years. Then find the kinds tasted at one, two and three a day, and compare each with one lakh.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: days in 100 years = 365 × 100 = 36,500; one a day gives 36,500 kinds
narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, multiply three hundred sixty five by a hundred, to get thirty six thousand five hundred days.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>With one kind each day, the total is also thirty six thousand five hundred.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, taste two kinds each day. Multiply thirty six thousand five hundred by two.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The total is seventy three thousand kinds.

marks.m1: 36,500 × 3 is written with a box for the total

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, taste three kinds each day. Multiply thirty six thousand five hundred by three.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>The total is one lakh nine thousand five hundred.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Taking one lakh away leaves nine thousand five hundred. Only three kinds each day pass one lakh.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the three totals
narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: 73,000 sits in a bubble beside Keeko; 1,00,000 − 73,000 = 27,000 is written and the 27,000 gap glows
narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Keeko thinks seventy three thousand is almost one lakh, so two kinds each day should reach it.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>But almost is not enough. Taking seventy three thousand from one lakh leaves twenty seven thousand.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Those twenty seven thousand kinds are still missing, so two kinds each day fall short.
